HDFC Bank deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha to step down on December 31
items.summary: Kaizad Bharucha has submitted his resignation as deputy managing director of HDFC Bank, effective December 31, 2026. This decision follows the Reserve Bank of India's approval for Anup Bagchi to become the new managing director. Bharucha has served as a whole-time director since June 2014 and would have exceeded the 15-year tenure limit by June 2029. His departure marks a significant leadership change at India’s largest private-sector lender.

India is fastest-growing polymer compound market, expected to grow to USD 16 bn by 2031: Crisil
items.summary: India is becoming the fastest-growing polymer compound market globally, contributing 13 percent of a USD 75 billion industry. The market is expected to grow significantly, reaching USD 16.5 billion by FY2031. Demand from the automotive and infrastructure sectors is driving this growth, alongside technological advancements in manufacturing. Significant expansion in electricity networks and pipelines is projected to fuel demand further.

items.summary: In a significant ruling, a Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration tribunal has turned down a ₹908-crore claim aimed at Tata Chemicals. The tribunal instructed Tata to compensate Allied Silica and its head with a payment of ₹1 crore, with a dissenting opinion from one member. Tata Chemicals is currently assessing the implications of the tribunal's award from October 15, 2026, as it strategizes its next steps.

Urban Company Q2 net loss widens to ₹182.48 crore; revenue up 41.4%
items.summary:
Home services marketplace Urban Company on Friday said its consolidated net loss widened to Rs 182.48 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27.
The company had posted a net loss of Rs 59.33 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.
Urban Company's revenue from operations rose 41.4 per cent to Rs 537.29 crore from Rs 380.03 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a sequential basis, the net loss widened from Rs 92.12 crore in the April-June quarter, while revenue was up 1.7 per cent.
The company's board also approved raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through the issue of equity shares or other convertible securities via qualified institutional placement (QIP), subject to shareholder approval.
The board also gave an in-principle approval to explore residential air conditioners as a new line of business under its 'Native' brand. The company said it already services millions of air conditioners every year, which gives it first-hand insight into product gaps and customer needs.

Urban Company Q2 net loss widens to ₹182.48 crore; revenue up 41.4%
items.summary:
Home services marketplace Urban Company on Friday said its consolidated net loss widened to Rs 182.48 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27.
The company had posted a net loss of Rs 59.33 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.
Urban Company's revenue from operations rose 41.4 per cent to Rs 537.29 crore from Rs 380.03 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a sequential basis, the net loss widened from Rs 92.12 crore in the April-June quarter, while revenue was up 1.7 per cent.
The company's board also approved raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through the issue of equity shares or other convertible securities via qualified institutional placement (QIP), subject to shareholder approval.
The board also gave an in-principle approval to explore residential air conditioners as a new line of business under its 'Native' brand. The company said it already services millions of air conditioners every year, which gives it first-hand insight into product gaps and customer needs.

items.summary: Biocon announced a settlement with Genentech over its biosimilar, Pebrilzo, of the cancer drug Perjeta. The agreement allows Biocon to launch Pebrilzo in early 2027 in the UK and EU, and in late 2028 in the US. In response to Genentech's patent infringement suit, the New Jersey court dismissed the case at Genentech's request. The details of the settlement agreement remain confidential between the companies involved.
